title: TriBinary: Binary vs Multi-Valued Logic (Balanced Ternary & Quaternary) GPU Simulation Laboratory
description:
TriBinary is a reproducible, open-source scientific simulation laboratory and gate-level benchmark suite comparing binary, balanced-ternary, and quaternary GPU architectures under identical microarchitectural templates and physical silicon budget assumptions.

Key scientific findings:

  • Pre-registered Hypotheses: Locked under git tag prereg-v1 with SHA-256 integrity verification.
  • H1 (Radix Economy): Break-even cell-cost multiplier is c* ~ 1.585x.
  • H2 (Arithmetic): Balanced ternary sign detection is 79-96% slower (refuted), while relational comparison is 20-24% faster (supported).
  • H2 & H5 (Effect Decomposition): Multi-SM benchmarks isolate software encoding overhead (GPU-BT, +58% energy) from native ternary hardware gains (GPU-T, -42.6% GEMM dynamic energy).
  • H4 (Noise Immunity): Demonstrates steep symbol error cliffs at sigma/V ~ 0.07 due to reduced voltage half-margins.
